name: RM-Bench Math
description: The math domain split of RM-Bench (THU-KEG), evaluating reward models on their ability to distinguish correct mathematical reasoning from stylistically similar but incorrect solutions. The largest RM-Bench split, testing whether math-oriented reward models reward genuine correctness vs. well-formatted but wrong derivations.
evaluation_method: reward model accuracy on subtle preference pairs for math responses; robustness to style perturbations
general_score_metric: reward model accuracy on subtle math preference pairs
typical_sota_score: ~65–80% accuracy; math RMs often fooled by formally structured but mathematically incorrect derivations
reputation: ICLR 2025 Oral; largest split of THU-KEG/RM-Bench; critical for evaluating math process reward models (PRMs) and outcome reward models (ORMs); widely used to study reward hacking in mathematical RLHF
notes: ICLR 2025 Oral. Math split of RM-Bench (THU-KEG/RM-Bench, arXiv:2410.16184). 529 instances — the largest of the four domain splits. Each sample includes a math prompt plus 3 chosen responses (concise, detailed plain, detailed markdown) and 3 rejected responses varying in style. Particularly important for evaluating PRMs trained on chain-of-thought math data. Full benchmark: 1,381 total instances across chat (183), code (228), math (529), safety (441).
